subject: Copywriting
title: Claude Hopkins: Scientific Advertising
description: A 60-second lesson on Claude Hopkins: Scientific Advertising.

hook.text: In 1923, Claude Hopkins wrote a 70-page book that changed advertising forever. He demanded proof, not creativity.

buildup.text: Hopkins invented the coupon—a trackable device to measure which ads actually sold. He turned advertising into science.

discovery.text: He tested headlines, offers, and images with split runs. The winning version ran; the loser died.

twist.text: Hopkins also invented the free sample campaign. He gave away Pepsodent toothpaste and hooked millions on brushing.

climax.text: David Ogilvy said nobody should be allowed in advertising until they'd read Scientific Advertising seven times.

punchline.text: Test everything. Hopkins proved that advertising is math.

quiz.question: What did Claude Hopkins invent to track ad performance?
